subject: gk
question: Which of the following is NOT a feature of India’s parliamentary government?

options.text: Presence of nominal and real executives
Membership of the ministers in the legislature

solution:
The correct answer is __**Dissolution of the Rajya Sabha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• In India’s parliamentary system, the Rajya Sabha (Council of States) is a permanent body and cannot be dissolved.
 
• The Rajya Sabha is a continuing chamber, which means it is not subject to dissolution. However, one-third of its members retire every two years.
 
• The dissolution of the Rajya Sabha is not possible as per the Indian Constitution, making it distinct from the Lok Sabha, which can be dissolved.
 
• This feature ensures that there is always a functioning legislative body in the Indian Parliament to perform its duties and responsibilities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Presence of nominal and real executives**

 
 
• In India’s parliamentary system, there is a clear distinction between the nominal executive (President) and the real executive (Prime Minister and the Council of Ministers).
 
• The President is the ceremonial head of the state, while the Prime Minister is the head of the government and exercises real executive powers.
 
 
 
• **Membership of the ministers in the legislature**
 
 
• Ministers in India are required to be members of either house of Parliament.
 
• If a minister is not a member at the time of appointment, they must become a member within six months to continue in office.
 
 
 
• **Majority party rule**
 
 
• India follows a majority party rule, where the party with the majority of seats in the Lok Sabha forms the government.
 
• The Prime Minister is usually the leader of the majority party or coalition in the Lok Sabha.
